pr.t: Serengeti - Wilde Geschichten aus der Savanne
pr.d: Das Land erholt sich nach dem Feuer, der Fluss führt Wasser. Während die Löwenjungen schutzlos den Gefahren der Savanne ausgesetzt sind, muss auch das Nilpferdbaby im Fluss das Überleben lernen. Sein Vater bleibt nach einem Kampf verwundet zurück.

pr.t: Serengeti - Wilde Geschichten aus der Savanne
pr.d: Die Suche nach einem Zuhause bringt Tragödie und Triumph mit sich, denn das Nilpferdbaby Mafuta sieht sich neuen Gefahren gegenüber. Krokodil Magamba verteidigt ihre Jungtiere und Duma, der Gepard, kämpft darum, Freunde zu finden.

pr.t: Serengeti - Wilde Geschichten aus der Savanne
pr.d: Während das Land austrocknet, haben alle Schwierigkeiten, Wasser zu finden. Die Flusspferde geraten in den schrumpfenden See und Nalla, die Elefantin, findet eine clevere Lösung, um den Durst aller zu stillen.

pr.t: Serengeti - Wilde Geschichten aus der Savanne
pr.d: Während die Tierfamilien der Dürre entkommen, kehrt das Land zu seiner früheren Schönheit zurück. Neues Leben wird geboren, alte Rivalitäten werden beigelegt und neue Allianzen werden geschmiedet.

pr.t: Himba, Buschmänner und Löwen - Wildnis- und Kulturmarketing in Namibia
pr.d: Ein Reisebus nähert sich dem San-Dorf Grashoek in Namibia. Ein Schild begrüßt die Besucher im Bushman Living Museum. Noch im Bus beginnen die Insassen zu fotografieren. Eine typische Szene - und doch hat sie wenig gemeinsam mit üblichen Szenarien im Kultur-Tourismus. Keine anstürmenden Kinderscharen, keine laufenden Frauen, die aufgeregt Handwerkskunst anbieten und auch keine jungen Männer, die gegen Entgelt ihre Dienste anbieten.

Klimaschutz beginnt im Regenwald. Die Regenwälder in West- und Zentralafrika gelten als Lungen der Welt. Nach Schätzungen von WWF werden bis 2030 rund 30 % davon verschwunden sein. In 50 Jahren werden voraussichtlich nur noch kleine tropische Waldflächen übrig bleiben. Diese Zahlen sind angesichts des steigenden Bewusstseins über die Bedeutung des Klimaschutzes für den Erhalt des Planeten dramatisch.

pr.t: Juwel der Elefantenküste: Afrikas Wunderland Isimangaliso
pr.d: 3280 Quadratkilometer am Meer mit Elefanten, Nashörnern, Büffeln, Löwen und Leoparden: Der südafrikanische Nationalpark heißt Isimangaliso, in der Sprache der Zulus schlicht Wunder. Der Küstenstreifen wurde 1999 zum ersten UNESCO-Weltnaturerbe Südafrikas erklärt. Isimangaliso bietet mit seinen ausgedehnten Feuchtgebieten, Sumpflandschaften, Savannen und Küstenwäldern eine unvergleichliche Biodiversität mit entsprechender Artenvielfalt.

pr.t: Die Magie des Leoparden - Ökotourismus in Südafrikas Wildreservaten
pr.d: Afrikanische Tierparks locken jährlich hunderttausende Besucher aus aller Welt nach Südafrika. Der Wildlife-Tourismus nimmt rapide zu und sorgt damit für das Entstehen von Boomtowns wie Nelspruit und Hoedspruit rund um den Krüger-Nationalpark. Heute leben hunderttausende Menschen zumindest indirekt von der Anziehungskraft des Safari-Abenteuers. Es wird gezeigt, wie die Verbindung von Luxustourismus, Umwelt- und Wildtierschutz zu sozialer Gerechtigkeit führen kann.

pr.t: Im Reich der Königselefanten - Das Tembe Wildreservat in Südafrika
pr.d: Der "Tembe Elephant Park", ein 300 Quadratkilometer großes Gebiet an der Grenze Südafrikas zu Mosambik, gilt als einer der wenigen sicheren Orte für die "Great Tuskers". Ein Blick auf die Elefantenbullen mit ihren gewaltigen Stoßzähnen genügt, um zu wissen, warum sie auch als Königselefanten bezeichnet werden. Das Wildreservat wurde von einem König gegründet, dem Vater von Inkosi Israel Tembe, dem heutigen Chief der Tembe.

Dr. Julian Fennessy versucht, die zunehmend bedrohten Giraffen zu retten. In einem Einsatz plant er zusammen mit einem Team aus Uganda, 20 der seltensten Unterarten der Giraffe zusammenzutreiben und über den Nil in Sicherheit zu bringen.

Morten Schumacher steht auf dem Zehnmeterturm eines verwitterten Freibads. Morgen soll er den Turm abreißen. Ausgerechnet er, dem dieser Ort mehr bedeutet als irgendjemandem sonst. Denn das Freibad steckt voller Erinnerungen an die Geschichte, die sein Leben verändert hat, an das Jahr, in dem so viel passiert ist. Er war damals 15. Zwischen erster Liebe, Freundschaft und der Trennung seiner Eltern gerät seine Welt aus den Fugen.

Ein Unbekannter legt Hauptkommissarin Ann Kathrin Klaasen eine weibliche Leiche auf die Fußmatte ihres ostfriesischen Einfamilienhauses. Bei der Toten handelt es sich um eine alte Frau, die der Täter elendig verdursten ließ. Immer tiefer zieht der psychopathische Killer die Kommissarin in sein perfides Spiel hinein, dessen Regeln sie noch nicht einmal kennt. Das Team um Ann Kathrin Klaasen arbeitet fieberhaft.

pr.d: Knapp ein Jahr nach dem Sturz Baschar al-Assads befindet sich Syrien in einer schwierigen Übergangsphase. Ein Jahr lang werden Menschen begleitet, die nicht nur um das tägliche Überleben, sondern auch um Gerechtigkeit, Identität und Zukunft kämpfen.

Plötzlich ist nicht nur die Polizei hinter Whitney her, sondern auch das FBI, das ihn als einzigen Zeugen um jeden Preis beseitigen will.

Vor etwa 150 Millionen Jahren ist der Urkontinent Pangäa durch Plattenbewegungen auseinandergebrochen und der Atlantische Ozean entstanden. Der nordamerikanische Kontinent, der bisher mit Europa und Afrika eine zusammenhängende Landmasse bildete, wurde abgetrennt. Durch die tektonischen Bewegungen und den großflächigen Ausbruch von Magma veränderte sich das Klima des neuen Kontinents, mit tiefgreifenden Auswirkungen für Flora und Fauna.

Die Entstehung Zentralamerikas ist in der Erdgeschichte einzigartig: Während die meisten Kontinente vor mehreren Milliarden Jahren entstanden sind, ist Zentralamerika erst 150 Millionen Jahre alt. Zwischen Nord- und Südamerika haben die gewaltigen Kräfte auf der Erdkruste einen winzigen Platz für die ozeanische karibische Platte geschaffen, die größtenteils unterhalb des Meeres verläuft.

Der südamerikanische Kontinent ist Symbol großer Kontraste und Superlative: Heimat der längsten Bergkette der Welt, des größten Regenwaldgebiets, des wasserreichsten Flusses, der trockensten Wüste und der beeindruckendsten Artenvielfalt.

Rachel ist 40 Jahre alt und kinderlos. Sie liebt ihr Leben mitsamt ihren Schülern in der Schule, ihren Freunden, ihren Ex-Freunden und ihrem Gitarrenunterricht. Rachel würde gerne ein eigenes Kind haben, aber ihr Gynäkologe warnt sie, dass ihr nicht mehr viel Zeit bleibt. Sie verliebt sich in Ali und bindet sich an Leila, seine vierjährige Tochter. Sie deckt sie zu, pflegt sie und liebt sie wie ihr eigenes Kind. Allerdings geht sie ein Risiko ein, wenn sie die Kinder anderer Leute liebt.

Es geht um die Opalküste im Nordosten Frankreichs, die an der Somme-Bucht endet. Dort haben der Fluss Somme und die Gezeiten ein einzigartiges Biotop aus Dünen und Salzwiesen geschaffen. Der Rhythmus des Meeres bestimmt dort das Leben der Menschen.
pr.sub: Die Baie de Somme und die Opalküste

pr.d: Frankreichs Norden ist geprägt von einer einzigartigen Landschaft. In Französisch-Flandern will ein Koch die Welt verändern. Der Film erzählt die Geschichte von den verschiedensten Menschen, die ihre Heimat lieben und um jeden Preis schützen wollen.

Mit dem Menschen, der mehr und mehr in andere Regionen einreiste, siedelten auch viele Pflanzen und Tiere um. Manche exotische Arten können ganze Ökosysteme aus dem Gleichgewicht bringen oder tödliche Krankheiten übertragen.

Vermehrt siedeln sich gebietsfremde Tiere und Pflanzen in ihnen fernen Ökosystemen an und schaffen es dort zu überleben und sich zu vermehren. Durch den globalisierten Handel können diese Arten zu einer Gefahr für die regionalen Ökosysteme werden.

Um 1750 hat sich Agnes in Oberösterreich gerade mit Wolf verheiratet. Doch ihr neues Umfeld und das Eheleben werden für die junge depressive Frau rasch zur Qual. Als sie eines Tages auf einem Schindanger eine hingerichtete und zur Schau gestellte Frau sieht, ist sie fasziniert davon. Tod scheint für sie der einzige Ausweg aus ihrem tristen Leben zu sein. Daraufhin tötet sie ein Baby, sie stellt sich und will die Todesstrafe erhalten. Denn Selbstmord kommt für die gläubige Frau nicht infrage.

Das Filmteam von Regisseur Xiaorui trifft sich im Januar 2020 in einem Hotel in der Nähe von Wuhan, um eine zuvor unterbrochene Filmproduktion wieder aufzunehmen. Die Dreharbeiten sind fast abgeschlossen, als Gerüchte über ein neues Virus die Runde machen. Ein Teil der Crew schafft es gerade noch rechtzeitig nach Hause, aber der Rest sitzt mit Beginn der Ausgangssperre im Hotel fest und hat nur noch den Bildschirm als Gesellschaft.

Sam has figured out how to win Rebecca's heart, through music. Cliff falls for the trainee Margaret after their romantic interlude, which leads to his truck being reported missing.
Carrie is turned on by Doug's imitation of his new Hispanic co-worker, Rico. He later becomes jealous of his own Rico imitation! Arthur tries to chronicle his own life story.
Carrie has Doug sign a card for his boss' twenty years at the company. When he opens the card he decides he wants Doug to participate in his banquet roast and Doug blames Carrie.
Doug is offended that Carrie wants him to lose weight. So he vows to lose thirty pounds and makes a remark that she wears too much make-up to settle the score.
Following a run-in with a bull, Robert is in a foul mood and Debra decides to get to the heart of the matter.
Ray pushes Debra over the edge when he suggests that a pill could alleviate all of her PMS moodiness.
Still reeling from his run-in with a bull, Robert loses his nerve at work and decides on a career change to something safer - telemarketing.
Frasier's former high school prom queen agrees to set him up with her attractive friend if he agrees to tutor her son, who in turn, agrees to study hard if Frasier sets him up with Roz.
Frasier comforts a man (Patrick Breen) whose wife abandoned him and took their four children with her.
The gang heads to the Caribbean, where Frasier begins to question his new romance with Claire (Patricia Clarkson).
After returning from a tropical holiday, Frasier is visited by the former loves of his life and must make an important decision. Meanwhile, Roz is hounded by Lana's frisky teenage son.

pr.t: Gordon Ramsay's 24 Hours to Hell and Back
pr.d: This Italian restaurant, in Swedesboro, New Jersey, is in debt and serving dreadful food - some that would result in food poisoning. Gordon arrives to give the venue some much-needed culinary education.
Channel 4's midday news summary.
Steve and Sally restore original Victorian cupboards at their seafront New Brighton reno, while Andrew and Mandy's green fingers uncover a forgotten sunken garden in Warwickshire.
Peter and Judy explore the fun side of the Florida Keys, while Holly juggles medieval business and pleasure on Florida's Gulf Coast. And fire captain David puts on an Easter egg hunt.
Colin Murray, Rachel Riley and Susie Dent host, with JB Gill in Dictionary Corner, as contestants race against the clock to pit their wits against vowels, consonants and numbers.

Laura Hamilton is helping Vicky and Tom, who are taking early retirement and making a permanent move to the coastal town of Lagos on Portugal's Algarve. With their budget of £235,000 they want a modern two-bed open-plan property.

Meeting Claire and Joe who are following in the footsteps of a medieval French knight. In Italy, heavy rain threatens to wash out Cesidio's harvest. And in France, Liz and Dave are investing in solar panels at Lac de Maison.

In Ceredigion, Stuart and Amy offer a great big slice of vintage Americana at their place. They get everyone revved up with an afternoon of electric biking, but are left eating dust after some cleanliness complaints in their feedback.
Sales executive and positivity professional Julie serves up a positively purple night. Julie may be manifesting positive vibes, but her violet visions leave one guest perplexed.

Paul and his daughter Holly are looking for a holiday home in and around the Spanish coastal town of La Duquesa. Leah Charles-King shows them what their £190k can buy. After a few places don't quite hit the mark, will Leah's wildcard pay off?
Channel 4's flagship news programme. With sport and weather.
Susan Murray, MP for Mid Dunbartonshire, sets out the Liberal Democrats' campaign for a new health centre in Milngavie.

Elise and Elliot have three young kids and need to move out of Elliot's parents' house and into a home of their own. It's up to Kirstie to help. And Phil's with Kim and Ralph, who want a taste of what they grew up with in Zimbabwe.

As accusations continue to escalate, Fran and the rest of the women face a crossroads: stand together, or crumble from within. Meanwhile, Graham Hunter exposes the women's backgrounds, and Vanessa's daring stunt leads to a showdown.
Blonde bombshell Jess drops a bombshell with her date. Psychic Barbara can't predict her own future. And Connor, London's youngest black-cab driver, hopes first impressions turn into a second date.
The finalists make citrus celebration cakes, crème brûlée doughnuts and a tribute to iconic British landscapes. Who'll be the zest and be crowned the series winner?
What do the Goggleboxers think of Black Mirror, Gladiators and The Apprentice? Also, Britain's Got Talent, The Great Celebrity Bake Off for Stand Up To Cancer and Casualty.
A father and son duo double date. A make-up influencer struggles to open up to his tall, handsome date. And a disco dancing widower seeks more than just a dance partner. .
La Galleria 33 (Part 2/2): The saga of Boston eatery La Galleria 33 comes to a dramatic conclusion as Gordon Ramsay gives restaurant owners and sisters Rita and Lisa an ultimatum.
Mama Maria's: Gordon Ramsay visits Mama Maria's, a failing restaurant in Brooklyn, New York, where owner John is overwhelmed by running a business that's become stuck in the past.

But the former CNBC anchor won't worry about ratings for her hourlong general news program, comparing that burden to "death." Instead, she'll concern herself with translating world events into relevant information for viewers, paying close attention to such topics as the Middle East and women's issues. "I want people to say that our show is smart. I want our show to be authentic", Burnett says in a promo. "I want our show to have courage". Left unsaid, of course, is that she wants her show to have a big audience, too.

Cricket macht es sich zur Aufgabe, Gregly zu zeigen, wie man neue Freunde findet.

Der ganze Clan bereitet sich darauf vor, Halloween gebührend zu feiern, während er mit einer unerwarteten Nachricht konfrontiert wird. Die ganze Familie erfährt vom Tod von Dede, Jays Ex-Frau und Mutter von Claire und Mitchell.

Phil erfährt, dass sein Unterricht möglicherweise ausfallen wird, wenn Paige, eine seiner Schülerinnen, kündigt. Er versucht, sie zum Bleiben zu überreden, während Luke mit ihr ausgehen will. Jay will einer flirtenden Schülermutter Grenzen aufzeigen.

J.D. trifft sich mit Carla, um über ihre Eheprobleme mit Turk zu reden. Doch nach ein paar Drinks unterläuft ihnen am Ende des Abends ein kleines Missgeschick. Dr. Cox versucht mit seiner Frau eine gemeinsame Linie bei der Erziehung zu finden.

Turk erfährt von Carla, dass sie J.D. geküsst hat. Er reagiert auf diese Nachricht sehr eifersüchtig. J.D. muss nun versuchen, Carlas Ehe zu retten, bevor es zu spät ist. Er wendet alle Mittel an, um seinen besten Freund zu beschwichtigen.

Eine alte Dame, die J.D. schon behandelt hat, kommt wieder einmal in die Klinik. Diesmal aber hat sie ernste Probleme, und J.D. muss ihr sagen, dass sie das Hospital nicht mehr verlassen wird. Sie muss wählen, ob sie künstlich beatmet werden möchte.

Turk rettet einen Mann in letzter Sekunde, der an einem Imbissstand zu ersticken drohte. Er würde am liebsten allen davon erzählen, aber er hat Carla versprochen, sein Ego etwas zu zügeln. Er geht sogar auf eine Wette mit Dr. Cox ein.

J.D. zieht endlich in seine eigene Wohnung und will das gebührend feiern. Aber Turk will lieber etwas mit Carla unternehmen, nachdem sie sich endlich wieder vertragen haben. Elliott teilt ihren Freunden mit, dass sie das Sacred Heart verlassen will.

Randy will für die Schulzeitung einen Bericht über umweltbewusste Firmen schreiben. Tim verspricht ihm, ein Interview mit seinem Chef von Binford zu organisieren. Doch wie Randy herausfindet, zählt er zu einem der schlimmsten Umweltsünder der Stadt.

Familie Taylor freut sich auf den gemeinsamen Familien-Urlaub mit geheimem Ziel. Jill ist damit beschäftigt, die Koffer zu packen, während Brad noch unter der Trennung von Angela leidet. Als Tim dann bekannt gibt, wohin es geht, sind alle sprachlos.

Jill wünscht sich ein eigenes Büro im Dachgeschoss, um ungestört arbeiten zu können. Darauf hat Tim nur gewartet und stürzt sich bereits in die Arbeit. Jills Bitte, den Ausbau schlicht zu halten, werden von Tim überhört.

Al erfährt, dass seine Ex wieder heiraten will und ist vollkommen deprimiert. Tim versucht ihn aufzumuntern und gibt ihm den Rat, mehr zu unternehmen. Daraufhin verbringt Al nahezu jeden Abend bei den Taylors.

Brad bekommt ein Fußball-Stipendium von einer Uni in North Carolina angeboten. Tim ist so stolz auf seinen Sohn, dass er sich sofort als sein Coach bereit erklärt. Um das Selbstbewusstsein zu steigern, sagt Tim ihm täglich, wie toll er ist.

Danielle and Jordan pull no punches as they relive their knockout boxing-themed wedding. Wrong kind of ring, Jordan! But has Danielle forgiven him?

In Liverpool, three couples compete with globetrotting menus from Italy, Thailand and the USA.

Alfonso Ribeiro hosts as home video clips capture funny, surprising and memorable moments. In a Halloween special, costumes malfunction and dogs get spooked.

The Kid Is All Right: Lisa befriends studious newcomer Isabel but is distressed when her new buddy runs against her in the campaign for class representative.

Yippee Ki Yay Melon Farmer: Barry is thrilled about celebrating Christmas at Lainey's house. Marvin makes a big promise to Adam.
Basketball!: Phil's been doing basketball training so that he can redeem himself at the annual charity game. Then NBA stars Charles Barkley and DeAndre Jordan turn up...
Pig Moon Rising: Mitchell accidentally knocks over an urn filled with Cam's beloved pet pig Lilly's ashes. Can he cover up his blunder?
Five Minutes: Mitch and Cam have five minutes to catch a flight, and Haley and Rainer are forced to re-evaluate their entire relationship in five minutes.
Frank's Wedding: Frank Dunphy's Roaring Twenties-themed wedding day is finally here, and to get into the spirit, Phil gets the Dunphy clan to show up in costume.
The Star of the Backstage: Marge gets nostalgic about her days as stage manager of her high school play and reunites the cast for a re-run. They say you should never go back...
Bart's in Jail!: When a phone scammer who's pretending to be Bart fools Grampa into giving away $10,000, it's Homer who's the real victim. According to Homer, anyway.
Treehouse of Horror XXXII: Another Halloween helping of spooky tales, featuring some chilling takes on classic films including Parasite, Nightmare on Elm Street and, er, Bambi.
The Wayz We Were: Evergreen Terrace becomes one giant traffic jam thanks to a new GPS app. Moe reunites with an old flame - and this time he's determined to not screw it up.
Frankie and Darren have a heart-to-heart and Theresa is desperate for answers. Meanwhile, Ant reaches out to Kathleen-Angel and the young couple give things another go...
Brand new series - Party: Ahead of the summer vacation, Janine throws the perfect end-of-year party for her colleagues and friends. Series finale.
My Brother's Keeper: Will is confident that he'll slam dunk a college basketball scholarship, until he learns the truth about his closest competitor.
Geoffrey Cleans Up: When Geoffrey discovers that his new love is an heiress, not a housekeeper, he can't ignore the gulf between their social positions and ends their romance.
Britain's sharpest armchair critics watch The Apprentice, Hunted, Corrie, The Underdog: Josh Must Win, Bridge of Lies, and the News on the Princess of Wales' cancer diagnosis.
The Goggleboxers tune in to Gladiators, Is It Cake?, Casualty, The 1% Club, The Yorkshire Farm, This Morning, BBC News on the cost of living, and more.

The chefs must cook their fish courses but with some exceptionally high scoring dishes in the regional heats, each chef will need to deliver perfection in order to see off the competition. The judges are joined by guest judge Tim Henman.

It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all eight chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judge Gordon Reid.

It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British number one and Junior 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon champion.
It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to night shift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.
The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.
The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

Ross is hoping to impress with 'Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

It is the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness, and Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils, while Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

The chefs cook their mains and, following the previous day's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her 'carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat 'A Spoonful of Sugar'.

The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four-course menus.

Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his take on a traditional healing recipe, 'Mum's Flu-Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's 'A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed.

After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's 'Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's 'For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with 'Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great-grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

It's the turn of three chefs representing the south-west, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time. The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their celebratory starters.

It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X-Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second-busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an 'Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his 'An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head-to-head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

Three chefs take to the kitchen in a bid to represent the north-west in the national final. They include Ellis Barrie, from the award-winning Marram Grass in Anglesey, Liam Simpson-Trotman, an accomplished pastry chef and co-owner of the 4 AA rosette Orwell's in Oxfordshire, and Craig Sherrington, who sharpened his skills working under top names including Eric Chavot and is now Chef Patron of Virginia House in Cumbria.

It's the fish course and the chefs are all gunning for tens. Craig pays tribute to a friend who has revolutionised hospital food in Morecambe Bay, while Liam is inspired by health advice his grandma gave him and Ellis is dedicating his dish to the staff who delivered his son Albert. With cod, mackerel, shrimp and cockles on the menu, which of the chefs will score highly?

Time for the chefs to cook their mains and the pressure is on. Craig is hoping to impress using two cuts of Dexter beef, while Liam prepares his take on a Bajan lamb stew and Ellis prepares four cuts of suckling pig. Liam meets his personal hero, Nola Ishmael OBE, who became the UK's first ever black Director of Nursing.

It's the dessert course and the last chance for the North West chefs to impress in a bid to make it through to the regional final. Liam is cooking 'Not So Hot Toddy' in honour of a friend who works night shifts in the NHS, while Ellis' 'Worth Their Weight in Gold' is dedicated to the staff who saved his brother's life and Craig's dish 'The Missed Celebration' pays tribute to his wife with an unusual Christmas concept.

The two highest scoring chefs from the week return to cook their menus again. Judging them are Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and Andi Oliver who are joined by Dr Jake Dunning MBE, an infectious disease specialist who has been recognised for his work during the West Africa Ebola epidemic.

Three chefs are doing battle to represent Northern Ireland. Tommy Heaney, Head Chef at the Great House Hotel in South Wales, is taken on by Shauna Froydenlund, Chef Patron at Marcus Wareing's two Michelin starred restaurant, and James Devine, the 2017 National Chef of the Year.

After a tense starter course, the chefs return to the kitchen to cook their fish dishes. James is making his elevated take on a fried chicken takeaway as a tribute to the NHS staff who care for his sister. Shauna is also taking inspiration from a personal connection with a tribute to staff from a facility in her hometown of Londonderry. Tommy is hoping to impress with a dish dedicated to the discovery of DNA.

In the paranormal realm, entities manifest and terrify in many ways, often demanding attention with their poltergeist activity which includes the bumps and noises that haunt people at night.

Throughout time, humans have honoured their dead in unique ways. The one thing they all have in common is the final resting place is spiritually sacred. So when the activities of the living lead to disturbing the dead, the results can be terrifying.

Around the globe, seemingly perfect towns and cities conceal tortured spirits within their walls. These souls are distorted by the trauma, with suffering and anguish inflicted upon them in life and death.
Cam and David both have a unique relationship with the land, and soon realise that ghosts share this affinity.
Both Annie and John heard about ghostly legends in the places they lived, but they never thought that one day they'd be part of them.
Nadine and Sharon are shocked to learn that the close bond they had with their parents continues from beyond the grave.
Lee and Christine's relationships with death make them susceptible to ghostly activity.
pr.sub: One Foot in the Spirit World

pr.d: A woman sees the ghost of a vaudeville performer in a Trenton theatre; a man comes face to face with the spirit of a young man who died in a tragic accident.
Brad is driven from his home and onto the road during a year-long battle with a ghost that pushes him to the edge of sanity.
A woman meets an unusual man in a diner; a trucker helps a mysterious colleague out of a storm, receiving a comforting message in return.
When Erin's family start to renovate their new country home, the house's long and storied past comes to light.
A young woman is possessed by a demonic entity; a boutique falls under the spell of a spirit.
Deana Rotondo is tormented by the ghost of a predatory man, and a couple make a shocking discovery.

Wayne Mallows gets way more than he bargained for when he buys a haunted B&B; a family's dream home turns into a nightmare for their teenage son; Linda Bogert buys the historic home of her dreams only to be attacked and possessed by evil entities.

A couple accidentally invites spirits into their home when they decorate their nursery; Julie Stuart falls in love with an antique dresser that turns out to be haunted; a couple opens the door for a dangerous spirit with a shocking identity.
Paranormal investigators tap into the history of one of Ireland's ghostliest spots as they find out who, or what, is lurking in the shadows of this terrifying fortress.
Paranormal investigator Erin Goodpipe heads to Harrisville, Rhode Island to get the bottom of the rumours surrounding the witch, Bathsheba Sherman.
Paranormal investigator Erin Goodpipe tries to see who haunts Old Arnold Estate.
pr.sub: Who is Haunting the Old Arnold Estate?

How do they build the fastest tractor in its class? How is the world-famous frankfurter made, and how do they craft wallpaper fit for a king.

pr.t: Find It, Fix It, Flog It
pr.d: In Gloucestershire, Henry and Simon unearth more treasures ready to revive. They pick up a Victorian yarn winder, and later they find mid-century sideboard.
How do they build Formula 1 racing cars? How is the Leatherman, America's best-selling multi-tool made? How do they create classic Finnish Aalto glassware.
Drew is at a 900 year old Abbey in Somerset where he hopes to strike a deal. Later, he travels to a pedal museum in East Sussex and takes a trip down memory lane.
Angus helps Claire Richards by taking a huge chunk of pop memorabilia to auction. And he finds a blunderbuss and chastity belt in Amanda Owen's home.
Modern-day treasure hunter Drew Pritchard goes for a climb at a 17th century mansion in Cambridge. Later, he visits a massive salvage yard where he encounters a tough negotiator.
Angus clears a garage packed to the brim with rare antiques. Plus, he meets a woman and her collection of valuable ceramic horses.
Ford Fiesta Supersport And Lotus Elise. The guys are in Dundee to view a Lotus Elise S1. Drew is furious at numerous modifications made to the car, including stickers and a wing.
Natasha Raskin Sharp goes head-to-head with James Braxton. Driving a 1967 Daimler Sovereign, the pair are shopping from Pontypridd to Monmouth.
How do they make anatomical models, jukeboxes, tortilla chips and spark plugs? Find out as more items are put under the microscope.
Sam prepares Glenn's classic Yamaha for Brands Hatch. Can gearing and suspension changes give the former champion the edge over a determined rival.
How do they recycle metal and make pencils and coffee? Find out as more everyday items are put under the microscope.
Teleshopping.
Richard is reunited with a car from The Grand Tour, the cogs battle to fix a wedding car, and the Smallest Cog race team returns to the track.
Teleshopping.
Woodworker Robin Johnson restores a huge kitchen dresser for dealer Karyn Sparks. Leather expert Martin Ashcroft works on a unique set of leather books.
Claire visits clock restorer Steve with a piece from her childhood. Next, John brings in his mum's teddy bear, can Julie and Amanda fix up this sentimental toy.
Drew checks out unlikely animal items at Edinburgh Zoo. And, he rummages through a historic textile mill in the Scottish borders for industrial furniture.
Powerboats are built to ride waves faster than cars on the road. The secrets behind Swiss watches are revealed. Workers create high-quality wallpaper.
The world's leading submarine rescue specialists from several countries participate in a training exercise. Workers manufacture all-wheel drive cars.
Drew mixes with aristocracy at a Cornwall estate and finds an amazing collection of classic cars. In Newark, he unearths a hoard of enamel signs for the oil industry.

Marcus and Linden suffer an injury that could end their road trip. The Dust Devils attempt to produce the biggest gold pour of the season so far.

The Bushmen feel the aftershock of severe flooding as mine shafts start collapsing. A hazardous buildup of dirt forces the Tunnel Rats to create a makeshift dump truck.

How do they make anatomical models, jukeboxes, tortilla chips and spark plugs? Find out as more items are put under the microscope.
How do they recycle metal and make pencils and coffee? Find out as more everyday items are put under the microscope.

Woodworker Robin Johnson restores a huge kitchen dresser for dealer Karyn Sparks. Leather expert Martin Ashcroft works on a unique set of leather books.

Angus uncovers a rare coin collection and some vintage hair cutting gear. An old sea chest proves to be a treasure trove at auction.

Natasha and James hit the antiques emporia of the Midlands, discovering tiny shops, little gnomes and a huge specimen of a rather famous bird.

pr.d: In 1945, Allied bombings devastated Germany. James Holland joins Dan Snow to discuss its impact on WWII.

pr.t: Heroes on Deck: World War II on Lake Michigan
pr.d: The US Navy trained nearly 15,000 pilots on Lake Michigan from 1942-1945, resulting in the sinking of more than 100 classic World War II fighters and dive bombers.

pr.t: Swordfish: World War II's Surprising Aircraft And The Raid That Changed History
pr.d: Fairey Swordfish was a tough WWII biplane, famed for torpedo attacks despite outdated design.

pr.t: Aircraft Carrier: Guardian Of The Seas
pr.d: Exploring the engineering feats behind the modern US nuclear carrier.

The documentary details the Bismarck's search and sinking, featuring naval historians and Angus Konstam.

After the devastating loss of HMS Hood, the Royal Navy became focused on one objective, sinking the Bismarck. The flagship of the German Kriegsmarine had not survived completely unscathed from the exchange with the Hood and HMS Prince of Wales.

pr.t: The Air War: The Escalation of Allied Bombing
pr.d: The filmmaker sheds light on the controversial bombing campaigns that were unleashed during World War II and explores whether they actually achieved their intended outcomes.

pr.d: A look at Hitler's bold plan during World War Two to send fighter planes into Manhattan skyscrapers for the psychological impact it would cause on the citizens in the United States and the world as a whole.
The unique stories of ten very different people who were caught up in the liberation of Europe from the grip of Nazi terror are interwoven.
The stories of 10 very different people who were caught up in the liberation of Europe from the grip of Nazi Germany during the Second World War.

Lieutenant Sander undertakes an arduous journey to Leningrad, revealing the harsh German east campaign of 'Operation Barbarossa'. He notes down his experiences in a diary that provides us a look at the attack on the Soviet Union.

Lieutenant Sander undertakes an arduous journey to Leningrad, revealing the harsh German east campaign of 'Operation Barbarossa'. He notes down his experiences in a diary that provides us a look at the attack on the Soviet Union.

On 6 June 1944, Allied forces undertook the largest air, land and sea invasion in history. On D-Day, more than 150,000 Allied troops stormed five assault beaches in Normandy, attempting to break through Hitler's Atlantic Wall.

pr.t: Wings: World War Two in the Skies
pr.d: In the early days of WWII, pilots and engineers fight to win the battle of the skies. They use Spitfires, Hurricanes, Zeros, Hellcats, Oscars, ME 109s and Flying Fortresses.

pr.t: Wings: World War Two in the Skies
pr.d: The Hell Hawks fight D-Day in the air. The Avenger torpedo plane blows Japan's largest battleship out of the water. Nazi super-weapons bring terror from above.
Technological innovations in U.S. naval aviation change the face of war.
Technological innovations in U.S. Navy aviation change the face of war.

pr.t: Unsettled History: America, China and the Doolittle Tokyo Raid
pr.d: Examining the Doolittle Raid on Tokyo from the perspectives of the children of the Doolittle Raiders and Chinese villagers who aided in their rescue.
On its 200th anniversary, a team of experts uncovers the hidden mysteries of the Battle of Waterloo. It marked the final defeat of Napoleon and was one of the bloodiest battles ever fought.
Richard III, whose body was recently exhumed, is linked to the deaths of two princes in the Tower of London in 1483. Experts consider his guilt.
pr.sub: The Princes in The Tower: Royal Blood

pr.d: The infamous Borgia family were devastated when favourite son Juan was murdered in 1497. Can modern experts crack the case and finger the killer?
pr.sub: Juan Borgia: A Death in the Dynasty

pr.d: Bradley travels to the tomb of Tutankhamun to unravel the mysteries of the rise and fall of Egypt's most famous royal dynasty.

Alice tells the story of Norman England by studying the history of Winchester, Britain's most Norman city. Alice attempts to storm a castle in chain mail, investigates the origins of modern surgery and tucks in to an appetising eel pie.
In Norwich, the UK's most Tudor city, Professor Alice Roberts learns about religious intolerance, uncovers the Norwich FC canary's origins and experiences humiliating Tudor justice.

In search of adventure, Andy dives into Britain's weirdest events. He chases cheese down a hill in Gloucestershire, bog dives in Wales, eats chillies in Dorset, navigates a homemade raft in Monmouth, and faces Vikings at Tintagel.
Professor Alice Roberts explores the Georgian era in her hometown of Bristol, from architectural gems to the world's first chocolate factory, backstreet gin and the horror of the slave trade.

Finds include the lost WWI training trenches on Salisbury Plain, Britain's first 'double henge', discovered just down the road from Stonehenge, where the evidence suggests our ancestors feasted and made sacred offerings as part of a visit to the ritualistic Stonehenge landscape, and luxury foreign goods discovered at Tintagel, the legendary childhood home of King Arthur.
The team is in the north of Britain where they uncover evidence of the first Roman siege in Britain, Scottish man-made islands and a famous monastery.

The death of the Queen's uncle, Prince George, Duke of Kent, in a plane crash in 1942 has never been fully explained. The mysterious circumstances surrounding the crash has led to accusations that the Prince has been airbrushed from history.

Following the course of the invasion, as Strongbow wins victory after victory. In 1171, Henry II himself arrives to take control of Ireland, and grants land there to settlers from Britain. Now, archaeology and cutting-edge science reveal their fascinating lives.

Professor Alice Roberts tells the story of Edwardian Britain by visiting Cardiff, which grew rich selling the coal that powered the Empire. Alice hears the stories of the Edwardian miners and their backbreaking and often dangerous work.

Professor Alice Roberts explores the English Civil War through the history of Oxford, the city at the heart of a battle between an autocratic king and his rebellious parliament. Oxford became the power base for Charles I and his royalist supporters.
Andy joins a team of Nessie experts to carry out the biggest search for the Loch Ness Monster in 50 years.
pr.sub: Scotland: The Search For The Loch Ness Monster

pr.d: Andy embarks on a mission to unearth the Cornish sites of King Arthur, before magnet fishing for Excalibur and visiting the grave of a legendary witch.

Alice Roberts follows the excavation of Iron Age Britain's most spectacular grave. A team of archaeologists in East Yorkshire have uncovered the remains of only the third upright chariot burial ever found in Britain.

A secret location in the Cotswolds, with all the hallmarks of a high-status Anglo-Saxon cemetery, gives up a very precious and fragile artefact. And at the site of Shaftesbury Abbey, Dr Naoise MacSweeney joins archaeologist Julian Richards in his hunt for the missing cloister.

Dan Jones explores the turbulent history of Carrickfergus, one of the most ancient castles in Northern Ireland and a stronghold that holds the key to understanding the tempestuous relationship between Britain and Ireland.

Situated high on a crag overlooking the river Forth, Stirling Castle has guarded the gateway to the Scottish Highlands for centuries. The residence of kings, armies and felons, its battle-scarred walls have witnessed savagery and chivalry, intrigue, alchemy, adultery and murder. Location filming, stunning aerial shots and reconstructions bring to life its turbulent history.
Professor Alice Roberts explores the Georgian era in her hometown of Bristol, from architectural gems to the world's first chocolate factory, backstreet gin and the horror of the slave trade.

Professor Alice Roberts explores British history through the stories of individual towns. Alice examines Britain in wartime by looking at the coastal town of Dover, a town that found itself on the frontline in the struggle against Nazi Germany.
King George V's death in 1936 was later revealed to have been hastened by his physician. What were his motives and did he also euthanise the King's sister?
Sordid speculation dogged the life of Prince Albert Victor - he was even a suspect in the 'Jack the Ripper' case. Discover the truth here.
pr.sub: Albert Victor: The Prince and the Ripper

pr.d: A recurring mine marker points the team east to neighbouring Harrison Lake as leads and legend line up; clues found in a 1950s article by an investigative reporter place a lost Spanish gold mine directly on Slumach's path.
pr.sub: The Journey to the Lost Mine

HobbyMaker Repeats.
Kurz vor der Geburt ihres Babys nehmen Daphne und Ian ihr bisher größtes Projekt in Angriff. Sie verwandeln den dreistöckigen Taubenturm in eine luxuriöse Hochzeitssuite.

Ein Spaziergang durch das Schloss offenbart jahrzehntelange Schäden und Vernachlässigung, die für Chip und Jo eine Herausforderung bei der Restaurierung darstellen. Doch sie sind entschlossen, die Architektur zu bewahren.

Jo entwickelt mit ihrem Styling-Team ihre Zukunftsvision für das Schloss und gibt maßgeschneiderte Kunsthandwerksstücke in Auftrag. Chip entdeckt, was gerettet und zu seinem ursprünglichen Glanz wiederhergestellt werden kann.

Jo entwickelt neue Farben, die von der hundertjährigen Geschichte des Schlosses inspiriert sind. Chip und Jo treffen wichtige Entscheidungen über Bodenbeläge und Fliesen im Innenbereich sowie über die Steinmauern im Außenbereich.

Ein unerwarteter Wasserschaden ist für Chip und Jo ein kostspieliger Rückschlag. Doch der Einbau wunderschön restaurierter Holzstücke und wiedergewonnener Fliesen aus Europa beginnt, die ursprüngliche Pracht des Schlosses wiederherzustellen.

Für die Renovierung des Schlosses haben Chip und Jo elf Monate veranschlagt. Von denen sind nun acht um, und langsam fügt sich alles. Die Decken im Erdgeschoss bekommen ihren Anstrich und im Obergeschoss werden die Lampen installiert.

Chip und Jo sind endlich mit dem dreistöckigen Schloss Cottonland Castle aus den frühen 1900er-Jahren fertig. Die Renovierungsprofis enthüllen ihr Design und teilen ihre Tipps und Tricks, wie man alte Baukunst mit modernem Komfort verbinden kann.

Tamara Day wird kreativ und renoviert ein Haus im Ranch-Stil der 1950er-Jahre. Sie aktualisiert die Fassade mit Kunststein und fügt eine weitere Etage hinzu. Doch durch unerwartete Umstände muss sie ihre Pläne und ihr Budget überdenken.

Tamara Day nutzt ihre Erweiterung im zweiten Stock, um drei neue Schlafzimmer in einem Ranch-Haus aus dem Jahr 1950 zu schaffen. Außerdem gestaltet sie einen massiven Schrank um, aber bei den Duschtüren stößt sie auf unerwartete Probleme.

Die neuen Eltern Val und Deanna aus San Diego, Kalifornien, sind bereit dazu, ein neues Zuhause zu kaufen. Sie werden aber durch Studentenkredite und hohe Hauskosten ausgebremst und entscheiden sich kurzfristig für ein Tiny House.

Ein junges Paar sucht ein mobiles Tiny House, um den steigenden Mietpreisen in Gilroy, Kalifornien, zu entkommen und mehr Zeit im Freien zu verbringen. Dadurch hoffen sie auch, sich endlich auf das Wichtigste im Leben konzentrieren zu können.

Die Modestylistin Alexandra aus Brooklyn ist bereit, die hohen Mieten in New York hinter sich zu lassen. Deswegen will sie mit ihrem Online-Bekleidungsgeschäft in ihrem eigenen Tiny House wohnen und es mit Rädern mobil machen.

MJ und Meri Sue wohnen seit Neustem in Austin, Texas. Dort wollen sie ihr Geld darauf konzentrieren, ihre Studiendarlehen abzubezahlen, um schuldenfrei leben zu können. Deswegen suchen sie nach einem Tiny House mit Platz für sich und ihre zwei Hunde.

Kurtis hat einen neuen Job ergattert, weswegen er bald seinen Wohnort wechseln wird. Er muss seiner Frau den Umzug nach Melbourne verkaufen. Die beiden sind sich außerdem nicht darüber einig, ob sie ländlich oder urban leben wollen.

Ezra verlegt sein Immobilien-Büro von Los Angeles nach Mexiko, wo er in Zukunft mit seiner Frau Sheryl arbeiten wird. Einen ersten Einblick in den dortigen Immobilienmarkt erhalten sie, als sie ein Haus für sich selbst suchen.
pr.sub: Willkommen in San Miguel de Allende

pr.d: Für Laura beginnt ein neues Leben - sie hat den Krebs besiegt. Mit ihrem Mann Patrick und dem gemeinsamen Hund fangen sie in London ganz neu an. Patrick sucht eine sehr moderne Immobilie, Laura hingegen etwas Klassisches.

Ein Paar wünscht sich ein glückliches, einfaches Freelancer-Leben in der mexikanischen Stadt Puerto Morelos. Doch kaum übertreten sie die Grenze mit ihren beiden Hunden, wird ihnen klar, dass der Umzug in ein neues Land erstmal auch Stress bedeutet.

Nicole und Tim lernten sich im Deutschkurs der Highschool in Michigan kennen. Während eines Austauschprogramms in der Nähe von München verliebten sie sich ineinander und in Deutschland. Jetzt wagen sie den großen Schritt und ziehen nach München.
Diese Sendung wirbt für verschiedene Produkte, die man sich bequem nach Hause schicken lassen kann.

Der Gewinn kommt für Ashley und Marcus aus Boston gerade zur richtigen Zeit: Als ein Sturm ihr Häuschen verwüstet hat, bemerken sie zufällig, dass sie im Lotto gewonnen haben. Nun können sie mit ihren sechs Kindern in ein großes Haus ziehen.
Karen und Rick wollen einen luxuriösen Rückzugsort finden, wo sie mit ihren Enkeln abhängen können.
Joe und Jessie sind aus ihrer Wohnung herausgewachsen und wollen ein Zuhause im Landhausstil finden.

Melissa und Phillip begeben sich auf Schnäppchenjagd nach South Padre Island, eine schmale Insel mit weißem Sandstrand im Süden von Texas. Die sechsköpfige Familie braucht viel Platz und wünscht sich einen Meerblick und die Nähe zum Strand.
Eine Mutter zieht mit ihren zwei Kindern ins Strandhaus nach Port Aransas, Texas.
Ein Paar erfüllt sich den Traum vom Strandhaus und findet ein neues Zuhause in St. Pete, Florida.

Eine Familie hat das palastartige Anwesen ihres Großvaters übernommen und freut sich darauf, das Haus für eine weitere Generation zu bewohnen, doch zunächst müssen Tamara und ihr Team es wieder auf den neuesten Stand bringen.

Tamara und ihr Team renovieren ein toskanisches Anwesen, das in den 90er-Jahren steckengeblieben ist, von Grund auf. Eine Entkernung des Interieurs und eine Neugestaltung des Gartens verwandeln ein schäbiges Zugwrack in ein modernes Meisterwerk.

Tamara und ihr Team verwandeln ein riesiges Untergeschoss in einen atemberaubenden Lebensraum mit Medienraum, Bar, Schlafzimmer und Fitnessraum. Sie modernisieren auch die Küche, die Speisekammer und den Lebensraum im Garten.
Sharon und Darren stellen sich endlich ihrer gefährlich überfüllten und geschichtsträchtigen Garage.
Die geschiedene Faye bewältigt ihre Trauer durch Einkaufen. Cheries Renovierung macht Stimmung.
Zum ersten Mal nimmt das Team zwei benachbarte Häuser in Angriff, die voller Unordnung sind.
Für diese Weihnachtsfans kann es rund um die Feiertage gar nicht genug Dekoration und Traditionen geben.

Nick reist in die geschichtsträchtige Küstenstadt Hastings, um Mike und seine vier Hunde zu besuchen. Gesundheitliche Probleme haben den einstigen Wanderer ausgebremst und seine Hütte versinkt im Chaos. Kann Nick sein Zuhause wieder bewohnbar machen?

Nick reist nach Kettering, wo ein Ehepaar mit zwei Kindern von seinem eigenen Zuhause überwältigt wird. Ihr Dreifamilienhaus ist überfüllt und chaotisch - so sehr, dass es nicht nur ihr Wohlbefinden, sondern sogar ihre Sicherheit gefährdet.

Nach einer Transplantation kämpft Elektriker Frank mit den strukturellen Mängeln seines Hauses, die ein früherer Auftragnehmer hinterlassen hat. Die Familie Holmes nimmt sich des Projekts an und setzt alles daran, das Haus sicher für Frank zu machen.

Two terraces near beautiful countryside in Prestatyn in North Wales and Darley Dale in the Peak District and a shop and flat in Folkestone in Kent are all sold under the hammer. All three properties need a lot of work and Martin, Dion and Lucy meet the new investors to hear their plans.

Martin, Dion and Martel follow progress on a trio of houses sold under the hammer. Martin is in Wallasey on Merseyside, Dion is in Porth in South Wales while Martel is having a look around a property in Ripley in Derbyshire. All the developments take longer than expected and not everyone sticks to their budget, so will any of them make a profit?

A chalet bungalow in a bad state of repair in East Peckham in Kent, a piece of land in Tredegar in Wales ripe for a housing development and an end terrace in Hartshill in Warwickshire bought by an engaged couple are all sold under the hammer. Martin, Dion and Martel meet the new owners. None of the projects run smoothly but will it be worth all the hard work in the end?

Martin, Dion and Martel meet developers who all have very ambitious plans for their auction buys in Littleover in Derby, Barking in Essex and Congleton in Cheshire. Ideas range from a two-floor extension, creating an extra home, and a radical rethink on the use of one of the buildings. But do any of the developers manage to realise their dreams?

A flood-damaged house in Carlisle is brought back to life, and work is carried out on a piece of land in Breadsall Hilltop in Derby, as well as a semi-detached house with a great view in Alsagers Bank in Staffordshire. All three lots were sold under the hammer and Martin, Dion and Martel follow progress on the auction buys.
A two-bedroom flat in London's East Ham, a couple of maisonettes in Liverpool with a view, and a terrace house overlooking allotments in Coundon in County Durham are all sold under the hammer.

A fire-damaged house in Upped Beedon in West Sussex crying out for some TLC, a semi-detached house needing modernisation in Walsall in the West Midlands, and a former barn in beautiful Kent countryside in Sutton Valence are all sold under the hammer.

A terrace house in need of lots of TLC in Crewe in Cheshire, a character-filled former woodman's cottage in Blackwell in the West Midlands and a small studio flat with a big city view in London's Poplar are all sold under the hammer. Martin, Dion and Martel meet the new owners to hear their plans for their auction buys.

A first-time buyer wants to make a lovely home from a terrace house in need of updating in Brompton in Kent, while a house in Workington in Cumbria is bought by a team starting out on property developing and two cousins have big plans for a big house and garden in Great Barr in the West Midlands. Martin, Dion and Martel tour the properties and meet the new owners embarking on their projects. But will any of them manage to turn a profit?

A three-bedroom semi in Doncaster, a plot of land in Kent's Herne Bay and a small flat in London's Edmonton are all sold under the hammer. Martin, Martel and Lucy talk to the new owners and hear their ambitious plans for the auction buys.

A bungalow near the coast in Dymchurch in Kent, a detached house in Glanamman in Wales and a terrace house in Thornton Heath in Surrey are all sold under the hammer. Martin, Dion and Martel meet the new owners to hear their plans to turn a profit.

A detached house in Strood in Kent, a prefab bungalow in Alvaston in Derby and a large three-bedroom semi-detached with an enormous garden in Caterham in Surrey are sold under the hammer. Martin, Martel and Lucy view the lots before hearing what the new owners have planned.

Martin, Martel and Lucy visit properties in Sandgate in Kent and Bolton in Lancashire as well as a plot of land in Enfield in London at the start of the projects, following the progress until they're finished.

It's a family affair as couples and a father-and-son team tackle renovation projects in Stoke, Liverpool and Birmingham. Bedrooms are added as well as an ensuite and plenty of new kitchens and bathrooms in all three terrace houses.

A small garden with planning permission in the heart of historic Canterbury in Kent, a generously sized flat in London's ⚽ [EPL] Crystal Palace and a beautifully maintained bungalow in the quiet village of Branthwaite in Cumbria are all sold under the hammer. Martin Roberts, Dion Dublin and Martel Maxwell meet the new owners to hear their plans, which include a new build, an extra bedroom and a possible loft extension.

A couple of terraces, including a traditional layout Langley Mill in Derbyshire, a three storey terrace cut into the side of a hill in Tylorstown in Wales and a grade two listed property in Milton Regis, are all sold under the hammer. Martin, Martel and Lucy talk to the new owners and follow progress on their developments.

Including a stunning renovation of a Grade II listed house in London's Camden which took more than six years to achieve. The other two projects in Coatbridge, Scotland and Bootle, Merseyside are much shorter but the new owners still hope to make a healthy profit.

Three couples take on three properties in Wednesfield near Wolverhampton, Sydenham in London and Chatham in Kent in the hope of making some money. All of the properties need modernising but for one couple there is a hidden and costly surprise.

A bungalow in Chelsfield, a shop with flats above it and a semi detached in Erith are sold under the hammer. Martin, Dion and Martel meet the new owners to hear what they have in store for their auction buys, with all of them hoping to turn a profit.
The trio look at a family home in Kent, a former bar in Llanelli in Wales and a terrace in Croydon, all sold at auction. Will any of the developers make a return on their investments?

A three-bedroom semi in Crewe, a top-floor flat in London and a terraced house in Oldham are sold under the hammer. All the owners are happy with the prices they paid, but will any of them be able to turn a profit at the end of the projects?

While developers in Croydon in Surrey and Donnington in Shropshire wrestle with whether to lose a bedroom each for a better placed kitchen or bathroom, two friends in Derby consider creating two more in their six-bedroom house.

pr.t: Bradley and Barney Walsh: Breaking Dad
pr.d: Bradley and Barney are well into their Australian road trip, and before they leave the beautiful Blue Mountains, Barney has an extreme challenge planned for his dad as they must traverse a ravine on a rope! The boys then head into the countryside and make a stop in the land of sheep, where they learn the art of shearing. Their road trip then takes them to a tiny town where they join the local community who've organised a mighty challenge that involves pulling a gigantic truck.

UFO sightings at Joshua Tree National Park lead to the invention of the anti-ageing machine, links to a powerful creature called Yucca Man, and to theories of alien-human genetic experiments that could enslave the human race.
Exploring acceptance of alien contact and advancements in technology capturing more unidentified aerial phenomena sightings; a look at whether they are seeking Earth's oceanic energy.
Images from 1998 hint at a satellite orbiting Earth, possibly the Black Knight detected by Tesla in 1899; Oumuamua's artificial path puzzles scientists in 2017.

John Lennon and May Pang claimed to have seen a UFO from their balcony in New York, and a sinister visitor to a remote nuclear missile launch site in Montana, which more than 40 years ago caused nuclear missiles to be disabled for 24 hours.
A UFO is recorded flying straight from the sky into the sea with no loss of speed. Plus, astronaut Neil Armstrong goes in search of an ancient extraterrestrial library in the Ecuadorian jungle.

When satellites spot a mysterious structure in North Korea, experts investigate if this sinister evidence points to a looming nuclear threat, and using cutting-edge tech, they reveal dark secrets from this strange place.
A time-travelling woman appears in a bathroom and Pagan worshippers sacrificed humans.
pr.sub: Time Traveller, American Stonehenge, Plant Perception

pr.d: A look at Death Valley boulders, mysterious dancing lights on Brown Mountain, and super-marathon runners in Mexico.
pr.sub: Sailing Stones, Brown Mountain Lights, Super Human Runner

pr.d: Soldiers encounter a luminous triangular-shaped craft in an English field, and witnesses report a metallic object hovering over water.
pr.sub: Triangles in the Forest and High Tide

pr.d: A silent, orange football-shaped object is spotted over Loring Air Force Base in Maine, and a Swedish farmer witnesses a crash into a lake.
A 10,000-gallon water tank is found to be empty after an object is spotted hovering over it, and amaranth plants wilt after a saucer-shaped craft hovers above them.
A policeman discovers an oval-shaped object without windows or doors, and a woman spots an aura of light surrounding a small tree.
pr.sub: Desert Storm and Room With a View

pr.d: In 1980, a UFO detected on military radar, landed near crucial NATO bases. A group of military personnel claim to have seen a shiny metallic object with coloured lights and hieroglyphic inscriptions.
pr.sub: Rendlesham Forest, Back from the Future

pr.t: Top 25 Alien Encounters: Ufo Case Files Exposed
pr.d: The recent revelation that the US Government has been actively investigating UFO sightings and encounters has opened a new chapter in the pursuit of truth behind Alien Visitations. Top 25 Alien Encounters explores some of the most mind-blowing.
A woman claims breast implants saved her life and a young man saves a woman.
pr.sub: Bullet Proof Boobs, Amazing Coincidences, Directional Cows

pr.d: A man survives six lightning strikes and a toddler freezes, thaws and survives.
pr.sub: Lightning Strikes, Human Hibernation, Chinese Anchors

pr.d: When a sinister cave is discovered in a remote corner of Iceland, experts uncover a secret underworld tunnelling to unknown depths, and using cutting-edge tech, they investigate if this strange place could hold secrets of alien worlds.

In the white ice of Antarctica, satellites discover a mysterious trail of sinister black objects, and when experts discover that it's moving, they use cutting-edge tech to investigate who or what is behind this strange phenomena.

In January 2008, a shadow was cast over the town of Stephenville, Texas, when a UFO passed overhead at supersonic speed. Craig and Sarah speak to an eyewitness and investigate a possible military cover-up of the incident.

In October 2017, astronomers observed the very first visitor from interstellar space, 'Oumuamua'. Craig and Sarah speak with SETI scientists regarding its origin, and the possibility of extra-terrestrial life.
Examining the possibility that UFOs may be from Earth.
A series of UFO sightings in 1947 propels the phenomenon to the world stage. The US Air Force concludes that UFOs may not be from Earth.
Mars, humanity's space frontier, once resembled Earth, and its barren landscape and newly found doorways raise existential questions.
A look at the physics of time travel and the possibility of UAPs being humans from the future.

Several UFOs suddenly appear above Swedish power plants and other places. Some believe that the country will soon be the target of an attack. A soldier claims to have encountered a UFO years ago and receives compensation from the US military.

A fleet of UFOs is filmed over the South China Sea, a 12,000-year-old archaeological site reveals carvings of alien, six-fingered humanoids, and a recorded confession claims that Albert Einstein made a secret visit to Roswell in 1947 to see a crashed UFO and its dead and dying occupants.

Over many years investigation into government sources and interviews with government insiders, Ron James argues that the presence of another, advanced extraterrestrial intelligence engaging with humanity is being suppressed.
Kru chases down a taped conversation with a man claiming to have found Slumach's gold deposit. Taylor attempts to decipher an old map.
The search for Slumach's gold sends the team 300 kilometres away into the heart of mystery and murder; back in Pitt Lake, an unlikely prospector arrives with a shocking claim.
pr.sub: The Troubling Tale of Bute Inlet Gold

pr.d: Ancient Egypt, a civilization millennia ahead of its time, may have had extraterrestrial help in building its masterpieces.
The world's military forces have come face-to-face with thousands of unidentified objects; military encounters between Earth's armed forces and UFOs.
Governments around the world investigate UFO sightings, but many of them keep it a secret from the public.
Old legends warn of flying cryptids who descend from the sky, but new witnesses connect this aerial aggression to something more alien in nature.
Adam, Gwen and Julie recall personal encounters with UFOs, before experts' theories are put in doubt when we learn that each individual has time missing from their encounters.
A giant carving of a strange creature appears in the Australian outback, and strange bright green lights illuminate the seas around Thailand.
A strange structure might point the way to a lost civilisation's fountain of youth. Also, bizarre marks across the eastern US leave experts baffled.

Dan is in the heart of the English countryside at Warwick Castle. While it appears idyllic today, for centuries it was a poisoned chalice to the Earls of Warwick who lived there and its walls echo with tales of betrayal, bloodshed and murder.
Kevin Sempé explores the bay of Saint-Pierre in Martinique, where ships smouldered and sank following the devastating volcanic eruption of 1902.
The prophecies of Nostradamus, from the French Revolution to the rise of Adolf Hitler, have long piqued interest - and according to him, the world will end in 3797.
Tucked away in a Runcorn industrial park is the most excavated monastic site in Europe, revealing a story of medieval knights, brutal murder and ancient disease.
A new report is made every 55 hours in Washington state, which is America's highest rate of UFO sightings per capita - but why are UFOs choosing to hover here?
From midair abductions to near-disasters caused by unseen enemies, experts examine if we are alone in the skies over Earth.
Alien abductees reveal details about the insides of UFOs and help researchers understand how aliens live and what they want from the human race.

Ominous feelings of dread often accompany what some residents of Anchorage, Alaska call the "trumpets of the sky." Experts delve into the exoplanet WISE 0855-0714 as a theoretical source for these harbingers of fear and discover that the life that may have evolved there is far from human.
On February 25, 1942, the skies over the sprawling city of Los Angeles erupt like a volcano. Anti-aircraft weapons fire wildly at strange targets.
Strange black holes appear near Egypt's pyramids, ruins in Peru suggest the Incas knew more than expected, and a mysterious red swarm invades a beach in India.
A ghost ship with links to the mob suddenly appears on a California beach. Plus, a lake believed to have magical healing powers holds clues to life on Mars.
Andy embarks on a mission to unearth the Cornish sites of King Arthur, before magnet fishing for Excalibur and visiting the grave of a legendary witch.

Look inside the lost tomb of King Thutmose II and get new clues about Egypt's pharaohs, then dust off stone hunting structures in Saudi Arabia. Visit a 1,200-year-old mosque buried in the Negev Desert and inspect a 30-million-year-old predator skull.

pr.d: An Infantryman encounters an otherworldly presence on a high-stakes training mission. An Air Force Officer sees unexplainable lights in the sky while on a top-secret operation in Jordan, and in Baghdad, a Marine is haunted by the sins of the past.

pr.d: Das James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop verändert unseren Blick auf das Universum. Mit seinem Infrarotblick durchdringt es Staub und Dunkelheit und macht verborgene Welten sichtbar. Die Doku untersucht gewaltige Stürme auf Uranus, energiereiche Jets junger Sterne und die ungewöhnliche Form des Südlichen Ringnebels. Webbs Entdeckungen zeigen, welche extremen Prozesse Planeten, Sterne und Galaxien prägen.
pr.sub: Strip the Cosmos: James Webb - Die Reise ans Ende der Zeit

pr.d: Die Dokumentation erforscht das All auf neue Art und Weise: Mithilfe von CGI-Animationen werden Planeten, Monde, Schwarze Löcher, Sterne und ganze Galaxien Schicht für Schicht enthüllt. Dadurch kann ihre Struktur und ihre Herkunft erklärt werden.

Wir lernen über die Aufgabenbereiche der Bundespolizei: zum Beispiel den Grenz- und Küstenschutz mit dem Einsatzschiff BP82 Bamberg, den Einsatz von Spezialkräften sowie die Aufgaben der Bundespolizeidirektion Flughafen Frankfurt am Main.
pr.sub: Die Bundespolizei - Zu Wasser, zu Lande und in der Luft

pr.d: Die Bundespolizei wird auf verschiedene Einsätze begleitet, um deren breit gefächerten Arbeitsbereiche kennenzulernen. Von Schutz am Flughafen bis hin zur Beweissicherungs- und Festnahmeeinheit wird der Alltag der Bundespolizei beleuchtet.

Die Correctional Institution for Women ist das älteste und größte Frauengefängnis auf den Philippinen. Die Bandbreite der Inhaftierten reicht von Kleinkriminellen bis hin zu Mörderinnen und Gangmitgliedern, die häufig aus dem Großraum Manila kommen.

In der von Armut und Arbeitslosigkeit geprägten Stadt Zenica liegt das größte und härteste Gefängnis von Bosnien. Seit vielen Jahren konkurrieren Katholiken, Orthodoxe und Muslime vor Ort um die Macht. Zenica gleicht daher einem Pulverfass.

In der Hauptstadt Manila befindet sich das größte Frauengefängnis der Philippinen. Die Großstadt ist von Armut gezeichnet, und viele Schicksale enden in der Kriminalität. Die häufigsten Vergehen sind Betrug, Prostitution und Drogen.

Der Zoll am Flughafen Atlanta findet im Gepäck eines angeblichen Partyveranstalters fast zwei Kilo der Vergewaltigungsdroge GBL. Am San Francisco International Airport macht sich ein Besucher des Burning-Man-Festivals mit zahlreichen Pillen.

In Honolulu gerät eine Frau ins Visier, die sich womöglich illegal in den USA niederlassen will. Noch brisanter ist: Ein herrenloser Koffer entpuppt sich als Drogendepot. Im Frachtterminal stoßen die Beamten auf eine perfide Schmuggelmethode.

pr.t: Vom Rind zum Steak - Europas größter Rinder-Schlachthof
pr.d: Täglich werden in Europas größtem Rinder-Schlachthof in Waldkraiburg circa tausend Rinder geschlachtet und weiterverarbeitet. Jedes Exemplar wird bewertet. Bei der Fleischverarbeitung wird ein strenger Produktionsablauf eingehalten.

Pro Kopf verzehrt der Deutsche 38,1 Kilogramm Schweinefleisch im Jahr. Die Dokumentation zeigt den Weg des Nahrungsmittels vom Tier bis auf den Teller. Ein Gutshof in Bayern setzt auf glückliche Tiere, Bio und Handarbeit.
pr.sub: Vom Schwein zum Schnitzel - Hinter den Kulissen der Fleischindustrie

pr.d: Der Burger ist ein beliebter Imbiss. Mittlerweile dringen immer mehr inhabergeführte Restaurants auf den Markt. Wie sieht es hinter den Bedientheken in deutschen Burger-Läden aus? Welches Geschäftsmodell überzeugt: Massenware oder Handarbeit?

Die moderne Küche soll schick, modern und repräsentativ sein. Dabei sind die Grundzüge der verschiedenen im Handel erhältlichen Modelle gleichermaßen einander ähnlich wie simpel. Küchen werden aus mehreren Schranktypen und E-Geräten zusammengestellt.
pr.sub: Die Küchenmacher - Von Maßarbeit bis Massenware

pr.d: Moderne Landwirtschaft ist ohne sie undenkbar: riesige Erntemaschinen. Die Reportage sieht sich auf der Messe "Agritechnica" um, ist bei einem Ernteeinsatz in Vorpommern dabei und zeigt, mit welchem Aufwand die Maschinen transportiert werden.
